subject.title: [Bug]: Concurrent allow-always approvals silently lose allowlist entries (last-write-wins race in exec-approvals.json)

question: Should the remaining fix be the broad cross-process locked mutation path in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78226, a narrower TypeScript-only allow-always repair, or a different approvals storage design?
rationale: The observable bug is clear, but the durable fix changes exec approval security-state persistence and fail-closed lock behavior across runtime owners, which automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Review the broad locked mutation path
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78226 as the current candidate, require exact-head proof, and ensure it covers this issue's concurrent allow-always race before closing this issue.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow TypeScript-only repair
options.body: Fix only gateway and headless node allow-always writes now, accepting that macOS and broader stale-writeback risks remain tracked separately.

options.title: Hold for storage redesign
options.body: Keep this and related approval-state issues open until maintainers choose a larger storage split or SQLite-backed approval-state direction.

recommendation.title: Review the broad locked mutation path
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78226 as the current candidate, require exact-head proof, and ensure it covers this issue's concurrent allow-always race before closing this issue.
